scope: Retry-chain persistence repair: stable policy-chain identity, contiguous per-policy attempts and one shared durable retry budget.
evidenceBasis: User supplied the exact llm/retry must keep one retryId per policy chain load error; the affected computer session log was not accessed.
The original generator allocated a new random retryId on every schedule, violating the released v4 relationship validator.
Regression fixtures run the actual native AgentLoop and full installed v4 catalog encode/restore for parent and child agents.

tests.countingNote: Node counts a parent test with subtests in its summary while JUnit emits its leaves; both original outputs are retained.

prevention: The recovery projection version is 2 so previous cached projections are rebuilt with per-policy identity and sequence.
Per-policy attempt numbers and retryId are independent of the total budget across policy changes.
Native retry-started events use the same policy identity and attempt as their schedule.
Full native history restoration is asserted after successful parent and child recovery, including 64 PI_AI_ERROR retries.
limitations: Existing corrupt history requires the separately delivered personal recovery utility; installing R38 does not rewrite it.
The affected remote session has not been available locally and its recovery must be confirmed on that computer.
This change does not alter UI; no new desktop visual acceptance or real provider request was performed.
No real local DSH installation, running task or user session was modified.
